figs.title: Cantilever wing modes and their boundary conditions
figs.caption: A clamped root holds deflection, slope and twist; a free tip carries zero moment, shear and torque. Bending frequencies rise in the ratio 1 : 6.27 : 17.5, and a load drives the mode whose shape it does work on: lift through the elastic axis drives bending, a moment about it drives torsion.

figs.title: Torque and tip twist with a touch point
figs.caption: Torsion segments along a span act as springs in series. When a junction touches a rigid stop, the inboard segment is held and the tip stiffness jumps to that of the outboard segment; a rubber bumper instead adds in parallel at the junction, giving an intermediate slope.

figs.title: Series and parallel stiffness in a two-material bar
figs.caption: Materials side by side share one strain, so their stiffnesses add (parallel, Voigt). Segments end to end share one force, so their compliances add (series, Reuss). For any mix the parallel value bounds the true stiffness from above and the series value from below.

figs.title: Indeterminate truss by the unit load method
figs.caption: Cut one redundant member to get a determinate truss. The real load opens a gap δ₁₀ at the cut, a unit tension pair opens δ₁₁, and compatibility closes it with δ₁₀ + Xδ₁₁ = 0. Any later deflection uses a unit load placed on the released structure.

figs.title: Guided two-bar column with two rotational springs
figs.caption: With the top guided on the vertical, the upper bar mirrors the lower one, so the mid spring C₂ turns through 2θ and stores four times the energy per unit stiffness. The load drops Hθ²/2, giving P_cr = (C₁ + 4C₂)/H, and the exact path P = P_cr θ/sin θ rises as a stable symmetric bifurcation.
